page: Amazon Web Services c8i.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz. The configuration provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage or GPU bundled with this instance, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring 2184.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 34.43 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25 percent. Conversely, multi-core and memory performance show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 4321.26 and the PassMark memory score of 1769.59 fall into the bottom 25 percent. Large block uncached memory read and write bandwidths remain average at 40.19 GB/sec and 31.2 GB/sec respectively.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c8i.xlarge offers a dense compute profile with DDR5 memory and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX, making it suitable for specialized vector and matrix operations without the overhead of a GPU. However, the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2 GB per core and weak multi-core scaling represent clear tradeoffs for memory-intensive applications. This instance is best suited for single-threaded tasks, text processing, lightweight web serving, and small-scale machine learning inference.
